note.label: THE REWARD OF THE RIGHTEOUS: WHO IS REALLY GETTING IN?

precepts.why:
How do we know we are the Israelites? “For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee. In all things have we trespassed, and not obeyed thy commandments”. We did not keep the commandments of God.

“Wherefore all that thou hast brought upon us, and every thing that thou hast done to us, thou hast done in true judgment.” God is righteous in what he did to us, because we had a choice and chose to break the commandments.

“And thou didst deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful forsakers of God, and to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world.” They hate the Lord. He delivered us to the most wicked in all the world because of our disobedience, and it was written. Look at the slave-breeding farms in Goodbye Uncle Tom, a girl handed over to be bred as soon as she was of age: that is how they did us. Esau is perverted.

moments.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears
Resetting Your Joy In The Lord

points: The three Hebrew brothers walked in the midst of the fire praising God, and Azarias prayed in the midst of the fire: blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers; for thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us. Imagine that: cast into the fire by Nebuchadnezzar, made eunuchs, the temple destroyed, and they said, thou art righteous in all that thou hast done to us; in all the things thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment.

For according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins. They understood that thing. We deserved what we got. Our people today have a hard time understanding that: for we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

points: Get Three Holy Children in the Apocrypha, or Prayer of Azariah as it says in some Bible apps, verse six.
For we have sinned and committed iniquity. Sinned and committed iniquity. Departing from thee. Departing from thee. Departing from our God.
So an evil heart of unbelief, and departing from our God, is when we pine away in our sin and iniquity. When we add sin upon sin.

But you see those certain signs and symptoms in people, and we will talk about that briefly. But we are also going to talk about the solutions, in order to reset your joy in the Lord, so you will not be overcome with that evil heart of unbelief.

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: What the three Hebrews said about Babylon was true back then and is truer for us today. “Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers”: they are in the fire, going through tribulation. It is what Spain called the auto de fe, the act of faith: during the Spanish Inquisition they burned the Black Moors and the black Jews alive if they did not become Christian. They got that from Babylon: if you did not worship Nebuchadnezzar’s idol, he threw you in the fire.

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us.” Imagine it: they are in the fire, and they say you are righteous for all you have done to us. This is what black and Latino Christians need to understand: everything that has happened to us in this country and wherever we are scattered, God is just. Slavery, tribulation, persecution, mutilation: we have deserved it and more. “True are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.”

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: “Thou hast executed true judgment.” It was prophesied that if we broke the laws this would happen; our people did not believe it, and we suffered the consequences. “For according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.”

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: “For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.” This is what many of our people will not confess. Christians will not take any accountability for what our forefathers did: we did not do nothing.

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: “In all things have we trespassed”: we broke all the commandments. “That it might go well with us”: that we might stay in the promised land.

commentary.passage: Song of the Three Holy Children 1:3-10
points: “Thou hast done in true judgment. And thou didst deliver us into the hands of lawless enemies.” If you thought ancient Babylon was lawless, this place is way worse: this is Babylon the great. At least back then we knew our identity, our own language and customs; this place destroyed everything from us.
“Most hateful forsakers of God”: what is worse, they have the Bible but will not obey it. “And to an unjust king, and the most wicked in all the world”: this place, the most wicked in all the world.
